register.name: Eight-year Government bond (LCG080834), Regional Government Securities Market
register.detail: Government of Saint Lucia · auction of 3 August 2026 · rate 6.95% · 32 bids · EC$50M offered · due 4 August 2034
register.note: Proceeds fund the budget as a whole and are not earmarked to any one standard
register.text: An eight-year bond of the Government of Saint Lucia, sold by auction on the Eastern Caribbean Securities Exchange through the Regional Government Securities Market, at a resulting rate of 6.95%. It funds the government budget as a whole, which carries the seven standards; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of them.

register.name: Saint Lucia Urban Resilient Flood Investment Project
register.detail: World Bank · International Development Association · approved by the Board 30 September 2025 · Castries, Anse La Raye and their river basins · project P504998
register.note: Almost 67,000 Saint Lucians expected to benefit
register.text: An IDA-financed project to reduce flood risk in Castries and Anse La Raye and their river basins, through drainage improvements, flood walls, green corridors and river restoration, with early warning and community coordination systems. It protects homes in low-lying areas, where nearly 60 percent of the population lives, and serves the shelter standard.

register.name: FISH-ADAPT: climate resilience for Saint Lucia’s fisheries communities (SAP053)
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · grant · approved 3 July 2025 · agreement effective 4 July 2025 · USD 3,158,997 disbursed 11 July 2025 · accredited entity FAO · total value USD 16.7M · to July 2030
register.note: Saint Lucia’s first single-country GCF project; 72K people projected to gain resilience
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant, implemented with FAO, for Saint Lucia’s fishers, fishing communities and coastal sea moss and aquaculture farmers: safer fishing operations, and boat ramps, jetties and processing sites made resilient to storms and sea level rise. It serves the food and livelihood standards in the communities that live from the sea.

register.name: Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Financing, with a Cat DDO
register.detail: World Bank · International Development Association · approved 10 April 2025 · Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option, a fast-access line of credit once an emergency is declared
register.note: Reforms: risk-informed physical planning, public asset management and a Disaster Risk Financing Strategy
register.text: A contingent credit that Saint Lucia can draw quickly once an emergency is declared, to prepare for and respond to natural hazards and health-related crises. It rests on reforms for safer land development, an inventory of public infrastructure and a new Disaster Risk Financing Strategy, and protects the shelter and health standards when disaster strikes.

register.name: OECS Skills and Innovation Project
register.detail: World Bank · International Development Association · approved 11 January 2024 · $30M credit to Grenada and Saint Lucia · $6M in grants to the OECS Commission · five years
register.note: One credit shared by Grenada and Saint Lucia; over 40,000 young people in post-secondary institutions across the OECS
register.text: An IDA credit to Grenada and Saint Lucia for investments in post-secondary education and innovation: stronger institutions, advanced technical and transversal skills training and a regional knowledge and innovation platform. It serves the education standard, for young people in post-secondary institutions and for at least 120 entrepreneurs and firms in the OECS region.

register.name: Sustainable Recovery Development Policy Credit
register.detail: World Bank · approved 11 January 2024 · project P179539
register.note: Reforms include the National Energy Policy and the Climate Change Bill
register.text: Budget support tied to recovery reforms: new fiscal, public financial management and procurement rules, the National Energy Policy and the Climate Change Bill. It promotes renewable energy, reduces reliance on imported energy and cuts costs, which serves the energy standard.

register.name: Theobalds and Patience water supply financing
register.detail: CARICOM Development Fund · two financing agreements, announced 25 July 2025 · US$4.2M concessional loan for Theobalds · US$781,000 supplementary loan for Patience · US$670,000 grant · executed by WASCO
register.note: CDF financing for water in Saint Lucia now almost US$7 million; over 45,000 people to benefit
register.text: Concessional loans and a grant from the CARICOM Development Fund to rehabilitate and upgrade the Theobalds and Patience water supply systems, restoring full treatment capacity at Theobalds and adding solar power, rainwater harvesting and public education on water use. It serves the water standard for more than 45,000 people.

register.name: Programme for Education, Realignment and Transformation – Saint Lucia
register.detail: Caribbean Development Bank · loan approved, announced 6 March 2025 · total cost just over USD 30M · CDB 56% · Global Partnership for Education USD 4M
register.note: A dedicated school for students with special needs, and existing schools retrofitted
register.text: A CDB loan to expand access to quality education: a dedicated school for students with special needs, existing schools retrofitted to modern safety and design standards, more early childhood development and inclusive learning, and teacher training in special education and psychosocial support. It serves the education standard, where 83% of young people complete lower secondary school.

register.name: Affordable housing financing facility
register.detail: Taiwan Eximbank and the St. Lucia Development Bank · signing announced 27 August 2026 · the Government of Saint Lucia as guarantor · EC$54M
register.note: Long-term mortgage finance for low- and middle-income households and first-time homebuyers
register.text: A financing facility between the St. Lucia Development Bank and Taiwan Eximbank, with the Government as guarantor, to expand affordable housing options for low- and middle-income households through long-term mortgage finance, with a focus on first-time homebuyers. It serves the shelter standard; on its approval in November 2025 the Government said the loans would also finance solar PV systems, drainage upgrades and water tanks.

items.name: The Forest

items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.2% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Diaspora
items.label: Of GDP sent home by citizens abroad, 2025
items.text: Citizens abroad send home a steady share of the economy: a flow that can back long-term finance.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: Helen’s Daughters
items.text: A non-profit that trains rural women farmers and runs a bi-weekly FarmHers Market in the north of the island, where women farmers sell their produce and artisanal products to around 300 patrons per market, with a tool library and yearly agricultural scholarships.

items.name: Black Bay Farmers Cooperative
items.text: A farmers’ cooperative in Vieux Fort whose packhouse, one of four rehabilitated and upgraded in 2026 by Export Saint Lucia and the Laborie Cooperative Credit Union with support from the Caribbean Development Bank, is now better positioned to carry its farmers’ produce from farm to market.

items.name: National Council of and for Persons with Disabilities
items.text: A non-governmental organisation whose aquaponics business in Vieux Fort, built with a 2022 grant so that people with disabilities contribute to food security, with raised beds spaced for wheelchair users, is run by four persons with disabilities.
